cases.title: The Phantom Login
cases.tagline: She was asleep. Her account was not.
cases.description: A marketing coordinator's account signs in at 3 AM from somewhere it has never been, and then quietly starts forwarding mail. Work out how the account was taken over, and what is just noise.
briefing: Northwind Analytics is a 120-person fictional analytics firm. At 03:14 UTC on Tuesday 10 March 2026 the security monitoring system raised a medium-severity alert: an unfamiliar sign-in for the account pnair (Priya Nair, Marketing Coordinator).
Priya says she was asleep. You have been assigned as the investigating analyst. Your job is to work out what happened, how, and what to do about it, using only the evidence in the case file.
All times are UTC. Some evidence is relevant, some is noise, and some looks alarming but is unrelated. You will be marked on how well your conclusion is supported, not just on the final answer.

entities.name: Priya Nair
entities.note: Account: pnair. Not a finance user.

entities.name: Finance share
entities.role: File share used by the Finance team

objectives.text: Work out how the attacker could have obtained Priya's password.
Understand the 03:12 login and why multi-factor authentication did not stop it.
Establish what the actor did once inside the account.
Separate real signals from noise (at least two decoys).

evidence.title: Email: "Mailbox storage full — verify now"
evidence.summary: Message delivered to Priya's inbox Monday evening, claiming her mailbox is nearly full.

fields.label: Subject
fields.value: ACTION REQUIRED: Mailbox storage full — verify within 2 hours

evidence.content:
Hello Priya,

Your mailbox is 98% full. Unless you verify your account within 2 hours, incoming mail will be rejected and your account may be suspended.

[ Verify mailbox ]
   Link text:   https://mail.northwind-analytics.example/verify
   Real target: hxxps://northwind-analytics-helpdesk[.]example/login   (defanged — never clickable)

Thanks,
IT Helpdesk

evidence.title: Browser record: form submitted to look-alike sign-in page
evidence.summary: Four minutes after the email arrived, Priya's laptop sent a form submission to the look-alike domain.
evidence.content:
17:43:31  GET   hxxps://northwind-analytics-helpdesk[.]example/login     200
17:44:12  POST  hxxps://northwind-analytics-helpdesk[.]example/login     302 -> https://mail.northwind-analytics.example/
17:44:13  GET   https://mail.northwind-analytics.example/                 200

evidence.title: Authentication log: successful sign-in at 03:12
evidence.summary: Account pnair signs in successfully from an IP and region never seen before, using a legacy protocol.

fields.label: Location
fields.value: Unfamiliar region (first time seen for this account)

evidence.content:
03:11:40Z  pnair  IMAP  203.0.113.58  FAILURE  reason=bad_password
03:12:07Z  pnair  IMAP  203.0.113.58  SUCCESS  mfa=not_applicable

evidence.title: Baseline: Priya's normal sign-ins (last 30 days)
evidence.summary: Where, when and how Priya usually signs in.

evidence.title: Failed-login burst across 40 accounts (Monday night)
evidence.summary: 312 failed sign-ins against 40 accounts from a single IP over 41 minutes.

evidence.title: Mailbox rule created: forward invoice and payment mail
evidence.summary: Six minutes after the login, a rule was created that forwards payment-related mail to an external address.

fields.label: Action 2
fields.value: Delete forwarded copy from Sent Items

evidence.title: File access: Finance share workbook downloaded
evidence.summary: The same session opened and downloaded a finance workbook Priya has never touched.

evidence.title: Statement: Priya Nair
evidence.summary: Priya's account of Monday evening and Tuesday morning.

fields.label: Reliability
fields.value: Consistent with logs where they overlap

evidence.content: "On Monday evening I got an email from IT saying my mailbox was full. I clicked the button and typed my password. The page just reloaded and my inbox came up, so I thought it was fixed. I was asleep at 3 AM. I did not set up any forwarding. I have never used the finance share."

evidence.title: Mail platform configuration: legacy authentication
evidence.summary: Shows which sign-in methods are allowed and where MFA is enforced.

evidence.title: VPN sign-in Tuesday 08:05 from a new IP
evidence.summary: Priya connects to the company VPN from an IP not in her baseline.

fields.label: Context note
fields.value: ISP outage notice posted for her area Tuesday morning

evidence.title: Email: IT password-expiry reminder (legitimate)
evidence.summary: A routine scheduled notice sent by the real IT team that morning.
evidence.content: Your password will expire in 14 days. Please change it using the staff portal.

evidence.title: Security alert SEC-2210: unfamiliar sign-in
evidence.summary: The automated alert that started this investigation.

fields.label: Rule
fields.value: Sign-in from a never-before-seen IP and region

learningObjectives: Recognise indicators of a credential-phishing email (sender domain, authentication results, link mismatch, urgency).
Read authentication logs and compare them against a baseline.
Explain why legacy protocols and missing MFA enable account takeover.
Identify post-compromise persistence such as mailbox forwarding rules.
Separate genuine indicators from background noise and unrelated anomalies.

verdictOptions.label: Credential phishing led to takeover of Priya's account by an external party
The attacker guessed the password through brute force or password spraying
Malware or a keylogger on Priya's laptop stole the password
Priya deliberately misused her own account
The alert was a false positive from legitimate travel or VPN use

cases.title: The Missing Blueprint
cases.tagline: The design left the building. Nobody can say how.
cases.description: A competitor's sneak-peek image looks suspiciously like a confidential gearbox drawing. Trace how the file became exposed, resist the obvious suspects, and be honest about what the evidence cannot prove.
briefing: Aerolume Robotics is a fictional 300-person robotics manufacturer. On Friday 17 April 2026 at 09:00 UTC, a rival firm, Vantor Dynamics, published a "sneak peek" image whose gear layout closely resembles the internal KESTREL gearbox drawing, the company's most sensitive design.
Engineering leadership wants to know whether the design leaked, how, and from whom. Several people have already been named in hallway gossip. You must work from the records, not the rumours.
Be careful: similarity between two drawings is not proof of copying, and access is not the same as intent. All times are UTC.

entities.name: Dev Malhotra
entities.role: Lead engineer, owner of KESTREL files

objectives.text: Establish how the file became exposed to people outside the company.
Work out who accessed it and whether each access was authorised.
Understand why the link was created (the business context).
Test the obvious suspects against the record (check at least three).

evidence.title: Incident report: competitor preview resembles KESTREL
evidence.source: Security inbox, report from engineering leadership
evidence.summary: The report that opened the case, with a similarity assessment from the lead engineer.

fields.label: Similarity
fields.value: Gear layout and several tolerance callouts match

fields.label: Caveat from reporter
fields.value: Fixture drawings show part of the same geometry

evidence.content: "The layout and callouts in Vantor's image look like our KESTREL v7 drawing. I can't tell whether they had the full CAD or only a partial drawing: our fixture drawings for the machining vendor show a lot of the same geometry. Please find out whether anything left the company."

evidence.title: File metadata: KESTREL_Gearbox_v7.cad
evidence.summary: Sensitivity, owner and current sharing settings of the confidential drawing.

fields.label: Current link setting
fields.value: Anyone with the link — can download (no sign-in required)

evidence.title: Sharing audit log: link created Thursday evening
evidence.summary: Who created the link, from which device, and where it was sent.
evidence.content:
19:40:05Z  SIGNIN   c-tbrandt  192.0.2.30  mfa=ok  device=LT-0412
19:48:22Z  LINK_CREATE  folder=/Projects/KESTREL/Release  scope=anyone  perm=download  expiry=none
19:48:50Z  EMAIL_SENT  to=quotes@ridgeway-machining.example  cc=sreyes@aerolume-robotics.example  subject="Fixture drawings for quote"

evidence.title: Link access log: who downloaded what
evidence.summary: Every download made through the public link, with source IPs.
evidence.content:
20:20:14Z  DOWNLOAD  Fixtures/Fixture_Drawings.zip   198.51.100.7   anonymous   UA=Mozilla/5.0 (generic)
22:10:41Z  DOWNLOAD  Release/KESTREL_Gearbox_v7.cad      203.0.113.91   anonymous   UA=Mozilla/5.0 (generic)
22:10:58Z  DOWNLOAD  Release/Tolerance_Stack.xlsx         203.0.113.91   anonymous   UA=Mozilla/5.0 (generic)

evidence.title: Email: Sofia Reyes asks for the fixture drawings
evidence.summary: The project manager's instruction to the contractor, before the link was created.

fields.label: Subject
fields.value: Ridgeway needs the fixture drawings tonight

evidence.content: "Tomas — Ridgeway needs the fixture drawings for quoting tonight. Please send them the Fixtures folder ONLY, not the full release. A link is fine. Thanks, Sofia"

evidence.title: Vendor onboarding record: Ridgeway Machining
evidence.summary: What Ridgeway is approved to access and from where.

evidence.title: Statement: Tomas Brandt
evidence.summary: The contractor's explanation of what he did and why.

fields.label: Reliability
fields.value: Consistent with audit log timestamps and email

evidence.content: "Sofia asked me to get the fixture drawings to Ridgeway. I right-clicked the Release folder, clicked Get link and pasted it into an email. I assumed it would only work for them. I didn't notice it said Anyone. I haven't shared the link with anybody else and I only found out about the preview from the news today."

evidence.title: Sharing policy configuration
evidence.summary: Default behaviour when staff or contractors create external links.

evidence.title: Access summary: Dev Malhotra (last 21 days)
evidence.summary: Dev opened or edited KESTREL files 214 times.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: Office network and managed laptop only

evidence.title: USB event: Elena Park's laptop, Thursday 18:20
evidence.summary: A removable drive was connected and a file was copied to it.

evidence.title: Badge log: after-hours entry at 21:50
evidence.summary: Someone entered the building after hours, 20 minutes before the external download.

fields.label: Reason on record
fields.value: Scheduled HVAC maintenance work order WO-2291

fields.label: Areas entered
fields.value: Plant room and loading bay only

evidence.title: Network log: repeated denied SSH attempts
evidence.summary: 40 failed SSH attempts against the file server overnight.

fields.label: Authentication
fields.value: Key-based only; no password logins accepted

evidence.title: Statement: Hana Voss, Ridgeway Machining
evidence.summary: The vendor's account of what they received and did with it.
evidence.content: "We got Tomas's email at about eight, downloaded the fixture drawings from our office and started quoting. We did not forward the link. I can't speak for every person on our team, so I'm happy to check our mail logs for forwarding if you give us two days."

learningObjectives: Read cloud-sharing audit and link-access logs.
Recognise how risky defaults and over-broad link scopes expose confidential data.
Separate accidental exposure from deliberate exfiltration using evidence of intent, scope and behaviour.
Test suspects against records instead of rumours, and discard red herrings.
State clearly what cannot be concluded (attribution of the external downloader, the preview's true source).

verdictOptions.label: Accidental overexposure: a public share link created for a legitimate vendor request was later used by an unidentified external party
Ridgeway Machining passed the link on to others
Tomas Brandt deliberately leaked the design
An outside attacker breached the file server
A staff member copied the design to USB
Dev Malhotra leaked the design

cases.title: The Locked Office
cases.tagline: Monday, 07:42. Every screen says the same thing.
cases.description: A small dental group arrives to find files locked and a ransom note on the screen. Reconstruct how the intruders got in, work out what can be safely recovered, and build a containment and recovery plan that does not make things worse.
briefing: Lakeview Dental Group is a fictional 26-computer practice. At 07:42 UTC on Monday 18 May 2026 the office manager found a ransom note on the reception PC. The shared patient schedule and billing files cannot be opened. The practice opens patients at 08:30.

You are the incident responder on call. The owner wants the schedule back immediately and is considering paying. Your job is to establish what happened, how far it spread, what can be restored safely, and what the team should do first, in the right order.

This is a simulation: nothing here is real malware. Pay attention to the sequence of events, the evidence you would need to preserve, and which instinctive actions would cause harm. All times are UTC.

entities.name: Dana Whitfield
entities.note: Found the note, runs the weekly backup rotation

entities.name: svc-vendor
entities.role: Service account for the practice-software vendor (MedSoft Support)

objectives.text: Determine how the intruders got in and how they gained control.
Establish the scope of the incident and what the attackers did before encrypting.
Work out which backups can be trusted for recovery.
Identify what executed the encryption, how it was launched, and why protections did not stop it.
Rule out the tempting alternative explanations (at least two).

evidence.title: Ransom note found on RECEPTION-PC
evidence.summary: A text note demanding payment and claiming copies of the practice's data were taken.
evidence.content:
YOUR FILES HAVE BEEN ENCRYPTED.
We also hold copies of your patient and billing data. Contact restore-desk@secure-mail.example within 72 hours or the data will be published.
Do not rename files. Do not contact the police.

(Simulation note: this text is fictional. It contains no real payment address.)

evidence.title: EDR alert: mass file modification on FS01
evidence.summary: An unsigned program began modifying files at ransomware-like speed on the file server.

fields.label: Action taken
fields.value: Detect only (prevention not enabled on servers)

evidence.content:
02:49:30Z  NEW_BINARY      svc_update.exe   unsigned  C:\Users\Public\
02:51:12Z  RANSOMWARE_BEHAVIOR  FS01  svc_update.exe  rename_rate=1100/min  action=DETECT_ONLY
02:51:12Z  ALERT_QUEUED  (email to unattended mailbox)

evidence.title: File server audit: scope of encryption
evidence.summary: Which shares were changed and which were not.

evidence.title: VPN log: svc-vendor signs in from a new IP
evidence.summary: A vendor service account connects from an address it has never used, with no second factor.
evidence.content:
2026-05-17 23:02:41Z  VPN_LOGIN  svc-vendor  src=203.0.113.140  mfa=none  result=SUCCESS
2026-05-18 04:07:12Z  VPN_LOGOUT svc-vendor  src=203.0.113.140

evidence.title: Directory log: privileges granted to svc-vendor on FS01
evidence.summary: The vendor account gained administrator rights on the file server and a scheduled task appeared.

fields.label: Event
fields.value: svc-vendor added to local Administrators on FS01

fields.label: Follow-on
fields.value: Scheduled task "UpdateSvc" created 02:47 to run svc_update.exe

evidence.content:
02:30:09Z  GROUP_MEMBER_ADDED  FS01\Administrators  member=svc-vendor  by=svc-vendor(remote)
02:47:55Z  SCHEDULED_TASK_CREATED  UpdateSvc  run=C:\Users\Public\svc_update.exe  by=svc-vendor

evidence.title: NAS01 log: backup snapshots deleted
evidence.summary: The online backup appliance lost its snapshots six minutes before encryption began.

fields.label: NAS01 domain-joined?
fields.value: Yes, reachable from the compromised account

evidence.title: Offline backup rotation record (Sunday 20:00)
evidence.source: Backup rotation checklist, signed by D. Whitfield
evidence.summary: The weekly backup to a disconnected disk completed and was locked in the safe before the intrusion.

fields.label: Media
fields.value: USB disk, disconnected after the job, locked in safe

fields.label: Connected to the network during the incident?
Practice open on Sunday?
fields.value: No, so little or no new data after 20:00

evidence.title: Endpoint inventory: which hosts are affected
evidence.summary: Indicators were found on four of 26 computers; three have no monitoring agent.

evidence.title: Patch log: Sunday evening update deployment
evidence.summary: A routine cumulative update was pushed to 24 computers five hours before encryption.

fields.label: Relation to svc_update.exe
fields.value: None: different path, unsigned, launched by remote session

evidence.title: Antivirus scan history: Saturday scan clean
evidence.summary: A scheduled full scan found nothing on any host.

evidence.title: Statement: Dana Whitfield, office manager
evidence.summary: What Dana found and what she did before calling you.
evidence.content: "I got in at 7:40, saw the message on reception and restarted that PC twice. It still showed the message. I opened the note on two other PCs to read it. I haven't touched the server. The offline disk is in the safe where I left it on Sunday night. Dr. Okafor wants to open at 8:30."

evidence.title: Email: Dr. Okafor, "Just pay"
evidence.summary: The owner's instruction to the office manager and IT.
evidence.content: "Just pay whatever they want. We have 40 patients booked today and I can't run the practice without the schedule. Get it back by 8:30, whatever it takes."

evidence.title: Firewall egress log: large outbound transfer from FS01
evidence.summary: FS01 sent about 4.2 GB to the same IP that signed into the VPN, just before the encryption.

evidence.title: Account report: former IT contractor jkarlsson
evidence.summary: The owner suspects a disgruntled ex-contractor. This is the status of his account.

learningObjectives: Reconstruct a ransomware incident from VPN, directory, backup, firewall and EDR evidence.
Explain why service accounts without MFA and excessive privileges are high-value targets.
Judge which backups are trustworthy and why offline copies matter.
Order containment, preservation, eradication and recovery steps correctly.
Resist pressure-driven decisions such as paying immediately or wiping evidence.
Treat attacker claims (such as stolen data) as unverified until the evidence supports them.

verdictOptions.label: Ransomware entered through the compromised vendor VPN account: isolate, preserve evidence, rebuild and restore from the verified offline backup, and do not pay
Ransomware confirmed; restore from the NAS01 nightly backups
Pay the ransom to get the schedule back quickly
A faulty Sunday software update corrupted the files
A former IT contractor sabotaged the systems
A storage hardware failure damaged the files

cases.title: The Insider Paradox
cases.tagline: Three accounts. None of them match the logs.
cases.description: A manager is certain a scientist stole research data. A colleague says she saw it happen. The scientist denies everything. The records disagree with all three. Decide what the evidence actually supports, and what it cannot.
briefing: Orion Biotech Labs is a fictional 80-person research company. On Thursday 11 June 2026 a data-loss-prevention alert showed 412 files from the LYRA assay dataset downloaded at night by the account jweber (Jonas Weber, Research Scientist).

His manager Claire Donnelly says she is certain Jonas copied the data to a USB stick in the lab around 10 PM. A colleague, Mira Ostrow, says she saw him there. Jonas says he was at home and never downloaded anything.

Nobody has done anything yet. Your job is to establish what the records actually show, which statements they support or contradict, and what cannot be concluded. Rushing to accuse someone would be a mistake with real consequences. All times are UTC.

entities.name: Claire Donnelly
entities.role: Research Manager, hiring manager for a pending promotion

objectives.text: Test each witness statement against the records that can check it.
Establish what the account and device actually did, and from where.
Determine why the data was pulled and where it went.
Separate motive speculation from evidence (check at least three).

evidence.title: DLP alert: after-hours bulk download
evidence.summary: The alert that started the accusation. It records what happened, not why.

fields.label: Rule
fields.value: More than 300 files from a restricted share in 10 minutes, outside business hours

fields.label: Destination
fields.value: Local disk of the managed laptop

fields.label: External transfer detected by this rule
Reviewed
fields.value: Thu 08:30 by SOC; line manager notified 08:45

evidence.title: Statement: Claire Donnelly
evidence.summary: The manager's certainty that Jonas copied the data to USB in the lab.

fields.label: Reliability
fields.value: Parts conflict with email, badge and device records

evidence.content: "I'm certain Jonas copied the LYRA data to a USB stick in the lab around ten last night. Mira told me she saw him. He's been secretive lately, ever since the promotion round started. I never asked him to do anything with that data after hours."

evidence.title: Statement: Mira Ostrow
evidence.summary: A colleague says she saw Jonas near the cold room at 10 PM.
evidence.content: "Around ten I saw Jonas near the cold room carrying a bag. I assumed he was copying data and I mentioned it to Claire this morning. I could be wrong, it was dim and I was in a hurry."

evidence.title: Statement: Jonas Weber
evidence.summary: Jonas says he went home and never downloaded anything.

fields.label: Reliability
fields.value: Denial of the download conflicts with access logs

evidence.content: "I left at six and went home. I haven't touched LYRA since Tuesday. I never downloaded anything last night. Why are you asking me this?"

evidence.title: Badge log: who was in the building on Wednesday night
evidence.summary: Jonas badged out at 18:05 and did not return before Thursday morning.

fields.label: J. Weber
fields.value: Badge-out Wed 18:05; no badge-in until Thu 08:12

fields.label: M. Ostrow
fields.value: Building entry 17:30; cold room door 21:58 (open 14 min)

fields.label: Tailgating possible?
fields.value: Not excluded by badge data alone

evidence.content:

21:58:03Z  OPEN   M.OSTROW  cold room
22:12:40Z  CLOSE  cold room (door sensor)

evidence.title: VPN log: jweber signs in from his usual home IP
evidence.summary: Remote sign-in with MFA approved on Jonas's enrolled phone.

evidence.title: File access log: 412 files downloaded over VPN
evidence.summary: The account jweber copied the LYRA dataset to LT-0733 during the VPN session.

fields.label: Matches request?
fields.value: "Full LYRA assay set" as in the Wednesday 16:31 email

evidence.title: Email: Claire asks Jonas to pull the dataset
evidence.summary: Wednesday afternoon, the manager asks Jonas for exactly the data that was later downloaded.
evidence.content: "Jonas, Halden need the full LYRA assay set by 9am tomorrow. Can you pull it tonight and upload it to the audit portal? Link is in the audit folder. Thanks, Claire"

evidence.title: Audit portal upload log
evidence.summary: The 1.8 GB archive went to the approved external auditor portal, and nowhere else.

fields.label: Account
fields.value: jweber, from LT-0733 over the VPN session

fields.label: Other external uploads from this session

evidence.content: 22:15:20Z  UPLOAD  LYRA_assay_full.zip  1.8GB  jweber  src=LT-0733  dest=audit-portal.orion-biotech.example  status=200

evidence.title: Device-control log: removable media Wednesday night
evidence.source: Endpoint device-control (all lab computers and LT-0733)
evidence.summary: No USB storage was connected on any monitored device between 18:00 and 08:00.

fields.label: Lab workstation USB ports
fields.value: Disabled by policy except approved devices

evidence.title: Device posture: LT-0733 location and activity
evidence.summary: The laptop was idle and off the office network until it woke at home.

evidence.title: HR note: pending Senior Scientist promotion
evidence.summary: Jonas and Mira both applied; Claire is the hiring manager; decision pending.

evidence.title: HR file: verbal warning from 14 months ago
evidence.summary: Jonas once received a warning for emailing a dataset to a personal address.

fields.label: Matter
fields.value: Sent a non-restricted dataset to personal email

evidence.title: Cold room log and sample withdrawal record
evidence.source: Cold room access and inventory system
evidence.summary: Mira herself was at the cold room at the time, retrieving samples in a cooler bag.

fields.label: Other badges at the cold room

evidence.title: Email: auditor confirms receipt
evidence.summary: Halden Compliance thanks Claire for the dataset delivered overnight.
evidence.content: "Hi Claire, thanks, we received LYRA_assay_full.zip via the portal at 22:16 last night and have started the review. Checksum matches. Pieter"

evidence.title: Browser history: searches on LT-0733 at 21:20
evidence.summary: Two searches that sound sinister when quoted on their own.

fields.label: Search 1
fields.value: "how to send large files to external auditors"

fields.label: Followed by
fields.value: Opened the audit portal instructions page

learningObjectives: Test witness statements against independent records instead of choosing a side.
Correlate email, badge, VPN, device, file-access and upload evidence into one timeline.
Distinguish motive, history and suspicion from evidence of action.
Recognise that a contradicted statement is not proof of lying.
Draw a conclusion the evidence supports while stating what cannot be known.
Recommend fair, privacy-respecting follow-up actions.

verdictOptions.label: An authorised, task-driven download with no evidence of exfiltration or misconduct; the conflicting accounts reflect inaccurate recollection, not proof of wrongdoing
Inconclusive: the statements conflict too much to conclude anything
An outsider used Jonas's account or laptop
Jonas stole the dataset
Mira and Claire deliberately fabricated claims to frame Jonas
